lessons.title: LEDs
lessons.introduction: Drive indicator LEDs safely with current-limiting resistors and clean blinking or PWM dimming logic.
objectives: Wire and program leds safely on Arduino.
Apply C++ functions, conditionals, and loops to real hardware.
Connect this lesson directly to its guided robotics project pathway.
conceptExplanation: Drive indicator LEDs safely with current-limiting resistors and clean blinking or PWM dimming logic.
Always verify power requirements, series resistors, common GND, and logic voltage (5V vs 3.3V) before powering a breadboard circuit.
lessons.analogy: Mastering leds adds another proven building block to your robotics engineering toolkit.

syntaxExplanation.summary: Applied Arduino C++ pattern for LEDs:
rules: Always share a common GND between power supplies and Arduino.
Use motor drivers for DC motors and resistors for LEDs.

codeExamples.title: Applied LEDs Sketch

lineByLine.code: void loop() { digitalWrite(LED_PIN, HIGH); delay(300); digitalWrite(LED_PIN, LOW); delay(300); }

lessons.realWorldApplication: Autonomous mobile robots, smart appliances, and educational robotics kits rely directly on leds.

commonMistakes.mistake: Powering motors directly from Arduino GPIO pins
commonMistakes.fix: GPIO pins supply only ~20 mA; always use an H-bridge driver and external battery pack.

commonMistakes.mistake: Skipping Serial Monitor verification
commonMistakes.fix: Print raw sensor values first before connecting actuators.

tryItYourself.title: m12_l01.ino
tryItYourself.challengePrompt: Adjust a threshold or timing value, download .ino, and test on your breadboard via Arduino IDE.
tryItYourself.expectedBehavior: Demonstrates reliable leds control on Arduino hardware.

exercises.prompt: Which engineering practice is essential when building with LEDs?
options: Drive indicator LEDs safely with current-limiting resistors and clean blinking or PWM dimming logic.
Connect motors directly to pin 13 without a driver.
Omit resistors on all LEDs.
Never connect GND rails together.
exercises.explanation: Drive indicator LEDs safely with current-limiting resistors and clean blinking or PWM dimming logic.

summary: Drive indicator LEDs safely with current-limiting resistors and clean blinking or PWM dimming logic.
Test sensing and actuation separately before combining them in a full robot.
